header.scope: Won: Daniel signed, but PayPal/Venmo handling and saved-card migration remain unresolved; the transcript does not say whether all markets or volume moved.
header.tag_why: The rep dates the win to an engineer's weekend prototype built from our docs and sandbox, after which Daniel stopped saying "if".

messaging_changes.current_line: Built for developers: launch payments fast with our APIs, docs and sandbox.
messaging_changes.change: For engineering-led buyers: "Get a working payout flow running in our sandbox before you commit. One customer's engineer built theirs over a weekend and demoed it at Monday standup." Offer the sandbox build early in every engineering-led evaluation, not as a closing step.
messaging_changes.why: The docs and sandbox were what landed, and the decision-maker stopped saying "if" after an engineer's unprompted weekend prototype, so the proof point should be a working build rather than the claim of speed.

messaging_changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
messaging_changes.change: For engineering-led companies maintaining their own payments code: "Payments shouldn't be a team. Stop babysitting your payments code and get your engineers back on the roadmap."
messaging_changes.why: Expansion was only the occasion; the pain was two engineers tied up keeping payments alive and a feature slipping three quarters, and the customer described it as babysitting a "haunted house" (exact speaker attribution of some quotes is uncertain).

messaging_changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
messaging_changes.change: Stop leading with the authorization-rate uplift for low-ticket marketplaces (for example, an average booking around $40). Keep it out of first-touch decks for this segment, and only bring it up if the buyer raises acceptance.
messaging_changes.why: The acceptance-rate slide met silence, and the buyer said that at a $38 average booking he was "not losing sleep over auth rates".

messaging_changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
messaging_changes.change: For buyers migrating from another provider or from in-house code, replace generic customer stories with two assets: (1) a named reference at a comparable size that migrated saved cards, stating how many cards were kept; (2) a one-page "what you keep and what moves" answer covering PayPal, Venmo and saved cards. Get both in front of the buyer before or right after their first competitor conversation.
messaging_changes.why: After the competitor call the buyer's question shifted to "what do we lose", and he asked who had done this at his size without losing cards, but that went unanswered, PayPal was deferred and Venmo still has no answer.

trigger.insight: Expansion was the occasion, but the pain was the cost of the in-house payments code: two engineers tied up and a sitter-pay feature slipping for three quarters. The buyer was shopping for relief from maintenance and a way to ship, not for global reach. The rep never says who they were paying before, so the incumbent is unknown.
trigger.messaging: Lead with 'stop spending engineers on keeping payments alive' and the cost of that upkeep, rather than M1's generic global-growth opener.

decider.insight: The engineering leader decided, with finance as a formality. The contradiction in the ledger is smaller than it looks: Daniel signed and also said finance would sign what he brought them, so the signature is his. The CFO's one question was about when sitters get paid, not cost, so no ROI case was ever tested with finance.
decider.messaging: For this buyer, write the pitch to the engineering leader and give them a one-line answer on sitter payout timing to carry to finance, instead of leading with M6's ROI study.

decided.insight: A working prototype did what no pitch did: it turned the evaluation from a bake-off into a build plan. The win was driven by engineering momentum, and it was won despite open PayPal, Venmo and saved-card questions, so those risks were accepted rather than answered. The 'risk they'd take' is the rep's read, not something the customer said.
decided.messaging: Make 'get a working payout flow in the sandbox before you commit' the evaluation motion, and offer it to every engineering-led prospect early.

gaps.insight: 'Nothing, really' was wrong: PayPal was deferred, Venmo is still unanswered, and the request for a comparable customer who migrated saved cards was never answered. The 'we'll find out' from the customer's engineer at kickoff shows this is still open after signing. The deal was won with these gaps, and they are now post-sale retention risk.
gaps.messaging: Build a named, sized saved-card migration reference and a one-page PayPal/Venmo answer, and add them to M8 proof instead of generic customer stories.

language.insight: The customer talks about relief from maintenance ('babysitting', 'haunted house') and a promise to sitters ('paid by Friday'), not infrastructure, marketplaces or payouts. 'The app' and 'sitter pay' replace our category words, so our vocabulary signals a generic vendor. Some quotes are attributed to Daniel by implication, so treat their exact source with care.
language.messaging: Rewrite M11 as 'Sitter pay that lands by Friday, without a payments team' and drop 'marketplace' and 'payouts' from first-touch copy for this segment.

gaps.question: Who was the incumbent, and what did Daniel's 'I've stopped learning their names' refer to?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Priya which provider the account manager complaint was about and what the in-house code connected to.

gaps.question: What did Braintree actually tell them?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Daniel or his engineer what they heard on the Braintree call and what moved them off it.

gaps.question: What did they ask for that we couldn't show?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Priya for the full list of unresolved items (Venmo, PayPal buttons, saved-card reference) and who owns each now.

gaps.question: Did the full scope (Canada, UK, existing volume) sign?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Priya which markets and what volume are in the contract.

gaps.question: Is the PayPal/Venmo risk actually accepted by the customer?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Daniel directly, through the CSM, what he decided on PayPal and Venmo.

close.rep_takeaway: When a buyer asks 'who's done this at our size?', answer with a named reference within a day; the unanswered question was still open at kickoff, and the prototype won you the deal, not your answers.
